question: The average weight (in kg) of a family of five members whose weights are 40 kg, 49 kg, 56 kg, 76 kg and 38 kg is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume a base weight of **50 kg** to calculate **net deviation**.

Deviations: (40−50), (49−50), (56−50), (76−50), (38−50) → −10, −1, +6, +26, −12.

Net Deviation = −10 − 1 + 6 + 26 − 12 = **+9**.

Average adjustment = Net deviation ÷ Total members = 9 ÷ 5 = **1.8 kg**.

Final Average = Base + adjustment = 50 + 1.8 = **51.8 kg**.

**∴ The correct answer is 51.8 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Weights of **5 family members** are 40 kg, 49 kg, 56 kg, 76 kg, and 38 kg.

**Formula Used:** Average Weight = (Sum of weights of all members) ÷ (Total number of members)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6c97b94953810ca91a7137b64e2dfc53c98265bc2071e9c578efc9a84ea43b48.png] 

Sum of weights = 40 + 49 + 56 + 76 + 38

⇒ **Total Sum** = 259 kg

Total number of members = **5**

⇒ Average = 259 ÷ 5

⇒ Average = 51.8 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 51.8 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of Averages

If a constant value **k** is added to all the observations, the new average will be **Old Average + k**. Similarly, if multiplied by k, the new average becomes **Old Average × k**.

Weighted Average Formula

When combining two groups with counts n₁, n₂ and averages A₁, A₂: Combined Average = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Net Deviation Principle

The sum of deviations of all observations from their **Arithmetic Mean** is always **zero**. This property is the basis of the shortcut deviation method.</p
